content.text:
**Finding: T4C — compliant (preferred position).**

§ 9.4 delivers the full preferred checklist:

| Preferred element | Where met |
|---|---|
| Customer may terminate Agreement or Order Form for convenience | § 9.4, first sentence ("in whole or in part") |
| ≤ 30 days' written notice | "upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor" |
| Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees | "Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date" |
| No Vendor convenience right in a committed term | "Vendor has no corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term" |

Cross-checks: §§ 9.1–9.3 are cause-based; § 9.5 preserves cumulative remedies; § 27.3 adds a force-majeure exit for Customer; § 24.4 bars a Vendor change-of-control termination; § 8.2 non-renewal runs only in Customer's favour (a RENEWAL item, not T4C). No early-termination fee or penalty is imposed anywhere.

Noted but not flagged here: § 2.1's three-year take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights" undercuts the economics of the § 9.4 exit. That is the minimum-commitment bargain and is handled under MINCOMMIT — flagging it again under T4C would double-count the same commercial term. No redline proposed.
